options.text: The current-carrying coil acts as a temporary magnet, and the iron nail makes it stronger.
The clips keep clinging after the current stops.
Putting the iron nail inside makes the electromagnet weaker.
The cold electromagnet cannot pick up clips until its nail heats up.

stem:
The diagram shows Ira's coil of insulated copper wire wound on an iron nail and joined to a cell. Steel paper clips cling to the nail tip.

Which claim about this arrangement is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: A powered coil behaves as a temporary magnet; an iron nail core strengthens it. Clips stop clinging when current stops; heating is not required.
teacher.figure_note: Coil on iron nail joined to a cell; clips at the tip.
